## 2026-11-14 — MCP as an object type in the Tools window

Reused the existing header of `tools.html` instead of building a second window: MCP is a
picker entry beside Local Folder, gated on the host capability (`sdeMcpServers`), not a
`VertexObjects` type - so the assistant's navigation contract and `normalize()` are
untouched and the ABAP object model keeps its name rules. The server goes in the existing
name field, whose match list serves the server names; the tools go in the existing
function picker, grouped with `<optgroup>` from the toolsets `overview()` already
computes. Eclipse bundles neither the page nor the capability, as with Object Navigator.

`mcp-external.js` gained `runTool(server, tool, args)`: it starts the server through the
existing `ensure()`, refuses a tool the server does not serve, and returns the server's
own answer untouched. `remember()` now also keeps each tool's `inputSchema` and its whole
description (`about`) beside the short catalog line, which is unchanged - the window needs
the schema to build a form, and nothing is started to read it.

`mcp.html` is the new page. The form comes from JSON Schema alone: `enum` to a list,
`boolean` to a checkbox (an option applied when the tool runs, not a toggle), `integer`/
`number` to a bounded number field, `object`/`array` to a JSON textarea, everything else
to a text field; `required` leads, the rest fold under Optional. An empty optional field
is not sent at all.

The result view is a list of probes over the MCP `content[]`, first match wins: image,
resource by MIME, a JSON array of objects as a table, an object carrying a row list under
`rows`/`data`/`items`/`results`/`records` as that table (the `columns` array orders it, the
scalars beside it stay as the counts and the statement that ran - the shape SelecTor, the log
report and `llmQueryResult` already read), other JSON as a tree, a fenced block as code in its
language, a text opening with `SELECT` as SQL (the same anchored test `logs.js` uses - no
reading of the text), and otherwise the server's text as it came, which is a view of its own
rather than a failure. A `Table | Raw` segment toggle - the shared `vertex-segment-toggle`,
used unchanged - redraws the same answer as the server's own text, so no view stands between
the reader and what arrived. Deciding by the shape of the answer, not
by a list of tool names, is what makes several hundred tools work at once and keeps a new
server from needing a code change.

Validation: five tests in `test/mcp-tool-window.test.js` cover the probes, a row list
carried under a key with its stated column order and counts, the controls built from a
schema, the page's own script parsing (no other test reaches it, since the page does not
use the shared Tools code), and `runTool` against a fake Streamable HTTP server including
its two refusals. Full suite after the change: 1590 tests, 1572 passed, 16 failed, 2
skipped - the same failure names as before this work, and the same count `dev_history`
already records for this repository. One failure during the work was this change (a sliced
`connect()` could not see the `mcpHost` constant) and was fixed by making the page bridge
test `sdeMcpRun` itself; `vertex-page.test.js`, the one that looked closest to this work,
was confirmed to fail with the change reverted. No baseline was captured before the first
edit, so the comparison is by name against the runs during the work and by count against
the recorded history. The page was checked in light and dark against a stub server: form,
both folds, busy state, every result view, and the Table/Raw switch. VSIX 0.9.92 rebuilt
and the packaged page matched its source. The window has been opened against a live ARC-1
server by the user; what that showed - the query answer arriving under `rows` - is what the
row-list probe and the switch were added for.

## 2026-11-13 — Release 0.9.90: Jev tool selection

Execution-mode follow-up: reused the existing Jev choice API to ask execution_mode beside the per-function and authorization questions. Task-wide descriptors include schema sizes. Direct is preferred, with uncertain staged choices falling back to direct; invalid choices stop before action. The direct path primes the existing guarded session with the same Jev result (no second decision or planning model), retains all selected task functions, and uses a 32-action task budget. SQL/code baseline and fixed authorization remain. Staged selection/JSON planning occurs only after a staged decision; its initial permission/cost accounting is carried forward. Task-wide explicit exclusions are respected. The mode is recorded in selection logs and the chat log. Corrected duplicated operation in PLAN_SCHEMA.required and added recursive uniqueness coverage. A real tool-free Codex gpt-5.6-luna smoke test accepted the corrected schema and returned a plan that parsePlan validated; SAP was not contacted. Validation: 140 focused checks passed; full run 1570 tests / 1552 passed / 16 failed, with the same failure names as the completed pre-change guard run (1566 / 1548 / 16). Tests cover one decision and no planning call in direct mode, five selected task functions surviving without truncation, staged routing before planning, missing/invalid mode decisions, conservative direct routing, permission propagation, and recursive schema-required uniqueness.

Stage-guard follow-up: the live Haiku run used 23 calls in its first stage and re-read five transports in the next. Added an operation enum to the JSON stage contract, narrowed broad ARC-1 actions before Jev and again on execution, and added a six-attempt stage budget plus a three-consecutive-failure stop. The request-local read cache keys canonical arguments and system identity, deduplicates concurrent reads, never caches failures, and is invalidated by writes. Cached attempts still consume the budget to prevent token-only repetition. Stage cancellation uses a local AbortController; a host guard produces a blocked report without falsely advancing, while user Stop remains global. One missing-capability retry can reselect within the same operation and authorization, preserving the remaining budget. SQL SELECT and source reading are now baseline functions (no Jev question); Jev adds at most one specialized function. Context includes configured SAP user/system/client instead of encouraging guesses from local email. Cache hits and guard stops are logged; Steps says tool calls. Reused the existing controller, accounting, schema compiler and log details. Validation: 136 focused checks passed. Full changed run: 1566 tests / 1548 passed / 16 failed; failing names match the prior completed JSON-plan run (1555 / 1537 / 16). An early baseline overlapped the schema-fixture update and contained three temporary operation-field fixture failures; these were corrected and are not counted as legacy failures. Read-cache tests cover concurrent deduplication, mutation races, system isolation and invalidation. Stage tests cover cancellation, fixed authorization, operation boundaries, budget exhaustion including cached loops and one bounded missing-capability recovery. No live SAP action was performed during this fix.

JSON-plan follow-up: the previous stage controller still relied on the executor volunteering transitions, and its first decision received the whole task. Reused the same executor's strict structured-output transport for a mandatory 1–6 stage plan, now parsed and validated before Jev or actions. A host loop drives each mini-task, requires a stage-ID-matching complete/blocked JSON report, and passes only declared dependency summaries to later stages. JSON plans and stage reports are logged with existing question/answer privacy switches. Each stage is a fresh API/CLI request; no static CLI tool-list workaround is needed for the managed path. Compact Jev descriptors omit full input schemas; stage selection ranks and exposes at most two permission-filtered functions. The original task supplies authorization only, not tools for future stages. Invalid/blocked stages stop advancement. No separate planner provider or fallback model is introduced. Validation: full pre-change baseline 1550 tests / 1532 passed / 16 failed; full changed run 1555 / 1537 / 16 with identical failing names. Final focused checks passed 126, including JSON-only planning, API/CLI host-driven stages, scoped dependency summaries, two-function caps and log privacy. JSON plan/stage details were visually checked in light and dark themes. For the recorded 26-tool task, catalog text fell from 89,507 to 10,485 characters and questions from 16,765 to 7,119; these are prepared-payload measurements, not live provider token savings. Multi-stage tasks get a tool-free final synthesis of their structured reports.

Staged selection follow-up: reused orchestrator-plan, the mutable request tool array, request-local MCP endpoints, Jev pacing/accounting and existing log reports. Added stable orchestrator_step / orchestrator_call controls so CLI clients with cached tool lists can obtain and invoke a new stage's tools in the current question. API clients also receive the replacement schemas on their next round. Each stage uses the original context plus bounded recent evidence; no separate planner or call before each action. Needed/maybe decisions and exclusions below 80% confidence are retained. Separate initial authorization decisions fix write/execution permissions for the turn; tools and broad ARC-1 actions are filtered and checked on every invocation, including the dispatcher. SQL reads remain available; no-run tasks block ATC, Unit and syntax execution. Selection is atomic, cannot overlap active calls, and is limited to eight stages with duplicate empty transitions refused. Each stage has its own Orchestrator tool selection log including retained uncertain and policy-blocked tools. Executor instructions now come from neutral host rules and selected schemas; raw ARC-1 and whole-server VERTEX tool guides are not forwarded. Cross-references to excluded tool names are removed from selected descriptions. A hidden-tool request in staged API mode returns a recoverable tool error, not a fatal request failure. Compatible-provider schemas are rebuilt each round even when the new set has the same size. Existing per-model budgets and cancellation are preserved. Validation: pre-change baseline 1538 tests / 1520 passed / 16 failed; full staged run 1545 / 1527 / 16, with exactly the same failure names. Subsequent transport/isolation fixes passed 120 focused tests, including a hidden SAPContext call followed by successful stage recovery; no live SAP call was made.

Reused jev.evaluate, review-jev connection/model selection, MCP process reuse, ai-accounting and Session Logs decision tables. orchestrator-plan now builds one bounded request with one include/exclude question per candidate; validates every answer and filters request schemas before API or CLI execution. The MCP wrapper exposes only VERTEX and ARC-1 candidates; previously enabled toolsets cannot leak in. Removed planner settings and supervisor. Decision failures stop before execution; cancellation propagates. Input logging respects existing question-log settings; the operation is a separate visible log type. Integration checks cover API/CLI filtering, cancellation, failure, MCP scope and per-tool decision validation. This orchestration is a VS Code capability; Eclipse receives the shared log viewer and synchronized release version. Verified VSIX 0.9.90 and Eclipse 0.9.90.20261113185846, with the local docs/ p2 site refreshed. The focused suite passed 117 checks and the log viewer was checked in both themes. Full suite: 1510 passed, 18 failed, 2 skipped; Separate HEAD 0.9.89 runs reproduce the existing UI, host coverage, accounting and Claude-agent failures; the remaining full-suite failures include local-provider diagnostics and an invalid-key Vercel fixture. No live SAP/decision-provider request was performed.

Per-model rate budgets on the same version. New model-budget.js holds a rolling 60-second window per provider+model carrying each request's time and input tokens, so one window answers both limits: tokens per minute from modelConfig[provider].limits and requests per minute from modelConfig[provider].calls. waitFor returns the longer of the two waits, and a call limit under 1 still lets the first request of a minute through, so a mistyped 0.5 cannot stop everything. Providers state different limits - Gemini refused a decision with "limit: 50000 input tokens per minute", a call-metered provider needs the other field - and a number left out is simply not enforced. It also holds a byte-based size estimate (4.24 bytes per token, measured on this project's orchestrator packets: 110,673 bytes were 26,098 input tokens), correct() to replace an estimate with the charged count, retryable()/retryDelay() for provider-stated delays, and paced() which waits inside the budget, runs, and on a retryable error whose stated delay fits WAIT_CAP_MS waits once more and asks the same model again. A request larger than the entire budget is not held back - waiting cannot make it fit. Non-retryable errors (invalid answers, oversized input, 404, Stop) are rethrown untouched. The budget is edited in the LLM Providers model table: In tok/min and Calls/min columns with a number field per row, read by model-config.rows() and saved into modelConfig[provider].limits and .calls beside enabled/known/unavailable, so no new setting or migration was needed. review-jev keeps thin wrappers over the module for the decision call sites; orchestrator-plan passes its connection and corrects the estimate from result.usage.input_tokens. Chat is paced too: openai-compatible.rateLimitedRequest waits before the first attempt of each round using an estimate of that round's messages and tools, and anthropic.ask does the same before each round; chat.js passes both budgets for the chosen model. The existing reactive 429 handling in rateLimitedRequest is untouched - pacing only avoids provoking it. Two earlier shapes were built and removed within the session: a stand-in decision model (a paid substitute answers a question nobody asked to move, and a silent model change would void cost comparisons) and a single global decision-only budget with one shared window (it charged one model's spending against another and did not reach chat models). test/toolset-rounds.test.js guarded the literal adjacency of 'apiTools = toolsNow();' and the request line in anthropic.js; the pacing block sits between them, so the guard was relaxed to the property it protects - the tool list is rebuilt each step before that step's request - with no behavioural change. New tests cover per-provider/per-model isolation, window arithmetic and the exact wait, the oversized request, estimate correction, error classification, delay parsing in all forms, the pre-call wait with its report, the single retry, and the table's persistence of budgets. Full suite: 1538 tests, 1520 passed, 16 failed - the same 16 as before this work, name by name. Eclipse is untouched. No live provider request was made from here.

Follow-up fixes on the same version. orchestrator-plan now exports connect(): the review-jev connection check lifted out of select(), which accepts options.connection and no longer resolves it twice. chat.js calls connect() before codeTools.orchestratorTools(), so a missing decision model costs no MCP server start; the refusal text is unchanged and lives in one place. model-config.clearUnavailable removes one model's entry from vertex.ai.modelConfig unavailable and checkModel calls it after a successful probe. That mark forces on:false, so a marked model can never be reached and could never heal through use: a re-check is the only moment it can be cleared, and the panel's own save already dropped cleared rows. Root cause of the vanished Gemini decision model: an older build probed models/gemini-decision-1 through generateContent and stored its 404; compatible.probe has routed that model to jev.evaluate since 0.9.89, so only the stored mark was left, and it both hid the row and held the row off, while vertex.ai.decisionModel still pointed at it - hence the orchestrator refusal. The developer's own settings were repaired directly, outside the repository. Three chat tests now mock orchestrator-plan.connect. New checks cover connect(), a supplied connection not being re-resolved, the mark lifecycle, and the hidden-forever case that reproduces the original defect. Full suite after the change: 1524 tests, 1506 passed, 16 failed; the pre-change baseline on the same tree was 1518 tests with 17 failures, and a name-by-name comparison shows no new failure. Verified VSIX 0.9.90 rebuilt and its packaged chat.js, orchestrator-plan.js and model-config.js confirmed to carry the fixes. Eclipse is untouched: orchestration and LLM Providers are VS Code capabilities. No live SAP or decision-provider request was performed.

## 2026-11-13 — Release 0.9.88: bounded tool results, failed-turn context and the conversation place

Fixed anthropic.ask ignoring options.images: the user message now includes native Anthropic base64 image blocks, with image payload bytes added to the transport budget as in the compatible provider. Regression verifies the serialized image and an attachment larger than the text-only budget.

Anthropic per-round usage now carries cost_usd calculated by the shared anthropic-pricing module (official list rates checked 2026-11-13). Total usage sums round costs; log-report and usage-report use the same fallback for existing Anthropic logs without changing files. Rates are list-price calculations, excluding account discounts; unknown models retain missing cost rather than borrowing another model rate.

New vscode/tool-result.js replaces the identical 24000-byte stub in anthropic.js, copilot.js and openai-compatible.js. bound() cuts a JSON list - a top-level array, or the objects array of an object - to 100 entries, then cuts whatever is still over 24000 bytes on a whole-character boundary; each cut appends its own note with the count left out and advice to narrow rather than widen. A string result (an MCP server's text content) keeps its JSON encoding, the cut applying to the text inside it. Evidence from the ALC session log of this date: six SAPSearch calls returned 118884 characters of object lists, of which the two largest (55805 and 25807 characters) were replaced by the stub - including the DEVC call that would have answered the question - and the request died on the size guard at model step 7 with a budget of 64000 plus 82410 bytes of tool schemas. The chat budget, which excludes tool schemas and images, rises from 64000 to 128000 bytes in anthropic.js and openai-compatible.js; the 64000 default of the small metadata requests is unchanged. chat.js now records the question of a failed turn in conversation, guarded by a recorded flag so a failure after the success push cannot duplicate it; a cancelled or superseded turn still records nothing, and no placeholder answer is invented. log-report marks a request_error detail as failed; log-report.html colours .entry.failed summaries with errorForeground, the rule placed after .entry .entry > summary so the nested-entry rule does not win on specificity. The kind filters lose their visible count, which their existing title already carries. Remaining limitation: 100 SAPSearch entries are about 20 KB, so several such calls in one conversation can still reach the 128000 budget - the note is what steers the model away from that. Verified by direct tests of bound() over the four shapes (long list, object with objects, small result, long non-list text) and by syntax checks; not yet exercised in the VS Code host, and no Eclipse update site was built.

session-log gains setContext, accepting only {mode:"folder",folder} or {mode:"sap",system,client?}; anything else is refused rather than written half, and the accepted value is stamped into every entry beside the conversation and branch. chat.js settles mode and working folder before the first log entry of any branch - they moved above the Web-search branch, which would otherwise log without a place - and derives the SAP system through topic-routing.scopeOf rather than repeating the active-system lookup. log-report reads the context back, trusting only those two shapes. The trap found while testing: render() regroups sessions by conversation into fresh objects, which silently dropped the context, so the filter would never have appeared; a group now carries the context of the first of its files that recorded one. The page offers a select of folders (shown by their own last path segment, full path in the hover) and systems with their client, each with a count, plus "Without context" when older logs are present, and only when more than one place is present at all. Measured before building this: of 383 local log files only 21 carried a place at all, inside topic-routing scopes, which is why recording it was necessary instead of deriving it. log-report.currentPlace derives the chat place the way chat.js derives it for the log (contextMode, chat.workingFolder, topic-routing.scopeOf for the active system). Session Logs keeps its full list and filters only on choice; its status line names the place shown. promptTable gives each question body a row of its own with a cell spanning every column, as the conversation list already did; previously lazyConversation was appended inside the first prompt-cell, which a fixed-layout table clamps to the Conversation column width - the answer text wrapped at about 250px whatever the panel width. vertex-task-visual gains a recognize scene in the same 1000x40 proportions and 4.8s cycle as the others, CSS only - a frame with grain, a sweeping beam and three detection brackets whose delays place them where the beam reaches them; chat.js marks the screenshot-recognition progress with that kind and the sidebar lists it among the scenes. Checked in both themes on the existing output/scene-preview stand, which inlines the real module. vertex-task-visual gains searchBand(text): the bits step aside in the middle of the band and the pattern is drawn there as SVG text, lit with the hit colour, escaped because it comes from a tool call the model wrote and cut to 28 characters to fit. searchWide is now searchBand(""), so a band with nothing to say is byte-identical to the old constant. chat-progress.subject names the pattern for Grep and Glob only - a read of a named file has no pattern - and chat.js sends it with the step, the page rebuilding the scene when either the kind or the pattern changes rather than taking the precomputed one. The conversation row carries the place under its question in a muted line, using the page own secondary-metadata convention rather than a new column, since the table is already wide. conversationList takes an optional place and the sidebar passes the current one, so the chat offers only its own conversations. The place is decided per conversation, not per file: a group takes the place of the first of its files that recorded one, so continuing an older unplaced conversation places the whole of it, with its earlier questions kept, instead of listing a stub of the new file alone. Covered by log-context.test.js (writing, refusal of bad shapes, reading back, refusing an untrusted shape in the file) and a page test for the filter. Full suite after this work: 1525 tests, 16 failures, the same 16 that fail on HEAD without these changes; the one test this work did break, the 64 KB request-limit assertion in toolset-rounds, was updated to 128 KB.

## 2026-11-13 — Topic views, SAP links and deferred log sections

sidebar adds a display-only native topic selector; it hides messages outside the selected/current topic and never changes routing or sends requests. Existing theme-aware controls are reused. SAP-name links walk rendered text/inline identifiers while excluding existing links, source blocks and controls. chat.openObject resolves untyped names with exact SAP search and QuickPick for ambiguous types; existing typed destinations retain their path. Direct navigation carries the last established topic into history, logs and the reply without invoking a model. listReport now sends section titles as light metadata. lazyConversation builds only those titles and waits for a nested toggle before requesting promptDetail, preserving the chosen opened section after hydration. Focused tests cover direct-navigation topic retention and exact-type disambiguation. Version unchanged.

## 2026-11-13 — Compact log actions and paged conversations

Removed per-row action cells in favour of a shared action panel populated on conversation opening. Table width is now 100% with a minimum derived from compact data columns and 250px for the question, instead of a fixed 1260px baseline plus reserved action width. promptTable renders 30 questions at a time; sortableHead accepts a data-sort callback so sorting reorders the complete conversation before showing page one. Real local log profiling: 276–278 conversation rows; opening the largest conversation fell from about 55ms to 24ms including forced layout (environment-specific browser measurements). ## 2026-11-13 — Stable log actions and lightweight resizing

log-report.html computes the initial minimum table width from column widths plus 350px for the conversation. The Actions column reserves 230px and is fixed; buttons remain on one line. Dragging only translates a fixed guide; column and table geometry update once on mouse release. ## 2026-11-13 — Recover topics and keep log tables responsive

topic-routing adds an explicit previous choice only for an unassigned previous exchange. Jev still decides whether it is a continuation or a new task; no forced inheritance. apply creates a stable topic using that previous question as its label. log-report column dragging freezes measured widths and changes the table width by the drag delta, avoiding fixed-table redistribution; action cells wrap and clip within their bounds. Step timelines and their note bodies are lazy. List payloads omit diff bodies and bound displayed questions, while the full text is retained on the host and fetched on opening. A prompt-key map avoids flattening all session prompts on each detail request. Regression tests cover the unassigned follow-up and compact list; browser checks in light/dark themes cover 135 questions, 1000 deferred model steps and an 80px drag with unchanged neighbours. Synthetic conversation expansion measured about 18–20ms; this is not a benchmark of the full live log folder. Version remains 0.9.87.

## 2026-11-13 — Route reviews by filenames without diff bodies

topic-routing observations strips the structured Review context attachment before constructing Jev state, extracting only distinct filenames; it uses the explicit reader refinement when present. Catalog and previous-turn evidence use the same extraction. git-history attaches explicit paths for single-file and all-file review scopes; code-review preserves them in the review envelope. Regression coverage verifies a multi-megabyte diff stays out of Jev input and audit state while remaining in the selected model history. This affects topic routing only, not explicit per-block Jev review/triage. Version unchanged.

## 2026-11-13 — Prepared context size in session logs

session-log measures instructions, prompt, tool declarations and answer schema before source omission, retaining exact UTF-16 length and a characters/4 token estimate. Numeric metadata is retained when request text logging is off. log-report parses the first recorded size per question separately from usage and carries it through lazy report lists. ## 2026-11-13 — Write access remembered per system, topic named once

mcp-external.js keeps the write answers in a map, server|system|client -> { setting: value }, held in globalState as vertex.mcpAccess and passed in from extension.js beside the catalog; accessValue() reads the triple first and falls back to the vertex.chat.*Access setting, which remains the default for an unanswered triple and is still what Settings shows. setWriteOption writes both. accessRemembered(server) answers whether this triple has settled every question that server asks, and sidebar.js asks only when it has not - except when the server picked is the one already selected, which is the way back to the window; the reselection is read before select() changes it. The three settings' descriptions now say they are defaults rather than the answer. Keying by triple was the user's call: without it, skipping the question would carry a sandbox's write permission to every other system.

sidebar.js plays the start scene for the automatic start too: on the webview's ready message, when a server is selected, is in the list and isRunning(name) is false, it posts the same mcpStart/mcpDone pair the manual path posts and joins the start already running — ensure() returns the live run or the pending promise, so nothing is started twice. chat-progress.js gained detail(name, input), used by both step reporters: the file (shortened to its last two segments when the resolved path is long), the pattern and where, the command, or the SAP object type and name.

chat.js:501 was the third place a step is reported - executeTool, which is how the API providers run SAP tools - and it named no scene, which is why those providers showed no animation; the two paths fixed earlier were Claude Code's stream and the /chat endpoint listener. The topic status now carries the id alone, and sidebar.js writes the topic into #topic-now in the Conversations summary instead of inserting a .topic-badge into every message; setTopic still sets the stripe and data-topic-id. ## 2026-11-13 — Waiting scenes for the chat's steps

Added search, mcp and edit scenes to org.vertex.abap.ui/resources/vertex-task-visual.js in the review strip's band (1000x40), sized by a new shared .task-band rule; colours come from --vscode-focusBorder, --vscode-testing-iconPassed and the gitDecoration added/deleted variables, so both themes follow the editor. The edit scene cannot be CSS alone: its cuts and insertions must fall at random, and a fixed loop reads as a blink every few seconds on a long request, so the module gained drive(node), which moves the row from JS, stops itself once the scene leaves the page, and leaves a still-turning helix where it is never called. The MCP scene is driven the same way and for the same reason: a round is a question pulsing out, the system thinking with its arcs, then a packet carrying real zeros and ones whose count differs every round. Both drivers degrade to a CSS loop when drive() is never called, so a host that only inlines the styles still shows a moving scene. chat-progress.js gained scene(name), the single mapping from a tool name to a scene: Read/Glob/Grep search, Edit/Write edit, Bash none, everything else mcp. chat.js reports it from onStep and from the /chat endpoint listener, assistant.js from Claude Code's own stream; a null scene leaves the running one rather than blanking the message for one step. sidebar.js carries all five scenes to the webview, accepts the new kinds, inlines the module after the page script so the script-extracting tests still find theirs, and starts the driver on the node it just drew. task-visual.js gained source() for that inlining. Rejected on the way: a scrolling helix (a seamless loop cannot also shift columns), a pen writing on sheets (too busy) and sheets folding into a document (needs a taller band than the chat allows). Two assistant tests were updated for the kind now sent beside the status. ## 2026-11-11 — The turning logo for every wait, and a timer beside the scenes (0.9.80)

The logo became shared, 32 px as in the chat (first 16 px, which the user found too small in Metrics): vertex-controls.css declares --vertex-logo as url("/*VERTEX_LOGO*/") and two classes, .vertex-busy (the logo before an element's text) and .vertex-logo-turn (the logo as an element), with their own no-motion rules. VS Code fills the marker through vertex-logo.js wherever it reads vertex-controls.css (tools window and its bundle, debugger, extension.js pages and the controls asset, code-review pages, log report, MCP window, LLM Providers, Path to This Line); Eclipse's PageView now fills it in .css as well as .html, so every view that reads the stylesheet through readResource has it.

(all of its waiting texts do), and every line of build progress; code-review.js draws the logo in place of the clock glyph of the "working" operation status (commit, push, PR, branch and now the build after Apply, which worktree-review.js sends as working, then success or error), keeping the glyph without motion.

The timer is part of vertex-task-visual.js: html() wraps every wide scene (install, start, wide review and commit, pr, push) with the timer beside it. It counts by CSS alone - two integer custom properties registered with @property, stepped each second and each minute by animations, shown through counters as mm:ss - so the scenes stay free of script timers; it pauses when the scene inside gets .scene-done (:has) and hides with the scene without motion. ## 2026-11-11 — The assistant's copy follows your own edits (VS Code 0.9.80)

Found in a session log (a free-model conversation on a C# player): gpt-5-nano broke channels.json in the agent working copy and left it undecided; the user fixed the file by hand in the folder, and could not apply the review (apply rightly refused a file changed during the review). Every later model - nano, codex-max, qwen - kept reading the broken copy ("the file starts with 1:", which the user denied), and codex-max "fixed" that copy by dropping CatalogKey and Headers, which the broken version no longer had. The copy was made once per conversation and never saw the folder again.

agent-worktree.js gains refresh(): the files changed in the folder against the starting commit, new in it, dirty at the start or decided since are compared, by blob id, with their base. A file the copy has not changed takes the folder's version; one with a change waiting for review is merged with git merge-file as apply already does; an overlap throws, naming the file, and leaves the copy untouched - the user decides the review first. The base moves to the folder's version, so the review measures the assistant's change against what the user now has. chat.js calls refresh() right after copyFor() on every turn and tells the model, in the review note, which files to read again.

The first writing of this put a real newline and a NUL byte into the code (escapes passed through a Python here-string); node --check caught the first, the NUL turned agent-worktree.js binary - both repaired before testing.

Validation: two new agent-worktree tests (an untouched file and a new file brought over; a waiting change merged, then an overlap refused with the copy unchanged); 15 working-copy tests and the chat test files passed. Not tried in a live conversation.

## 2026-11-09 — Direct schemas for orchestrator results (0.9.73)

Planner and recovery results use a direct root object schema with goal, context, steps, recovery and completion_checks; answer review uses a separate accept/feedback schema. Available tool names constrain its schema dynamically; local validation rejects forward/cyclic dependencies, wrong numbering, unknown tools and missing per-step criteria. JSON strings nested in answer are rejected. Both contracts are validated locally, with at most one retry for a format error or explicit unsupported structured-output mode; ordinary network errors, explicit refusals and invalid schema definitions are not format retries. All reported model usage, including malformed attempts, is accounted for.

## 2026-11-09 — New catalog models arrive switched off

A provider offers in chat only the models ticked in LLM Providers. A model added to a provider's catalog later used to be offered at once; it now shows in the table marked **new** and stays off until ticked, and the VERTEX panel says how many new models are waiting, with a link to LLM Providers. At the user's request (no silent selection of models nobody ticked) every provider now stores `enabled` plus `known` (the catalog ids at the last save); `rows` marks `isNew` / `missing`, `apply` leaves out `missing`, `news` gives the panel the new count and a dropped chosen model. `adopt` converts an old `hidden` setting once from the catalog read at that moment; `rows` throws if called before. `load` in the table no longer clears a chosen model that left the catalog. `listModels(fresh)` re-reads the catalog when the panel becomes ready. A review the VERTEX chat itself ran on the first cut found a lost-update race: the table loads every provider at once and each `adopt` rewrote the whole `modelConfig`; adopts now run through a queue (test added). Test fakes of `vscode` gained `ConfigurationTarget` and `update`; the test that required a dropped CLI model to be deselected now requires it to stay chosen. ## 2026-11-08 — No short retry for exhausted daily quota

OpenRouter free-model daily quota errors stop immediately instead of waiting a minute. A reported zero daily remainder also prevents retries for free routes. Temporary rate limits retain bounded retries; paid models are not blocked by exhausted free quota.

## 2026-11-08 — Keep transport failures out of model history

A successful Vercel answer repeated an earlier OpenRouter 429 because the technical error was saved as an assistant turn. Failed requests remain in diagnostic logs but are excluded from live model history and Session Logs continuation.

## 2026-11-08 — Model changes cancel rate-limit waits

Switching model or provider while chat waits to retry a rate-limited API request cancels that wait and releases the request slot. Conversation history is preserved; the next submitted question uses the new selection. The old retry cannot run or replace a newer answer. OpenRouter remaining daily free requests also refresh during rate-limit waits and on request errors; missing counters remain explicitly unknown.

After the generated RAP service the model could not publish binding Z_VX2_API_SFLIGHT_O4: SAP ADT's MCP server leaves SRVB actions to the editor. `abap-adt-api` has `publishServiceBinding`, but with the OData V2 address fixed in it. `vscode/sap-code.js` gets `bindingState` (the binding's ADT document: OData V2 or V4 from its category link, `srvb:version`, `srvb:published`) and `publishBinding`, which posts `publishjobs` or `unpublishjobs` to the address of the binding's type and reads the binding again. ## 2026-11-08 — API request limit leaves room for MCP tools (0.9.71)

The user's screenshot: with SAP ADT picked and OpenRouter as provider, the first question after the plan answer failed with "VERTEX: request exceeds 64 KB". The guard in `requestJson` (`vscode/openai-compatible.js`) and `request` (`vscode/anthropic.js`) counts the whole request body, and SAP ADT's tool definitions alone are about 93 KB, so no request with that server could pass. The guard is meant for the conversation and context, which grow; the tool definitions are fixed, so their size is now added to the limit. `test/toolset-rounds.test.js` sends 100 KB of tool definitions and checks the request fits while the conversation keeps its 64 KB. Copilot has no such limit.

## 2026-11-08 — Page copies made read-only; Session Logs changes restored (0.9.71)

The user's screenshot of Session Logs still showed a table as pipes after installing the build. `vscode/resources/` is not a source: `copy-pages.js` (vscode:prepublish) copies the pages and libraries there from `org.vertex.abap.ui/resources/`, the Eclipse bundle, and the folder is git-ignored. The table rendering and the **Continue in chat** button had been written into the copy of `log-report.html`, so packaging overwrote them and neither reached the VSIX; the earlier previews read the copy and passed. Both changes are now in `org.vertex.abap.ui/resources/log-report.html`. That page is also Eclipse's, which has no chat to continue, so the button shows only when the host sets `window.vertexCanContinue`, which `vscode/log-report.js` injects with the page's nonce.

To make the mistake fail where it is made, `copy-pages.js` leaves every copy read-only (it clears the flag before overwriting). The first build with that showed vsce storing each file's mode in the VSIX (`0444`), which would install read-only extension files, so `package.js` runs vsce with `VERTEX_PACKAGING=1`, under which the copies stay writable, and runs `copy-pages.js` again afterwards. Checked: no read-only entry under `extension/resources/` in the VSIX, the packaged `log-report.html` has the button and the tables, and the working copies are read-only (writing to one is refused). The removal of the copies after packaging was considered and set aside: `log-report.js`, `log-snapshot.js`, `model-config.js`, `tools-window.js`, `code-workbench.js` and `value-origin-view.js` read the copies with no fallback to the originals.

## 2026-11-08 — Continue a conversation from Session Logs (0.9.71)

The user asked whether a session could be resumed from the log, and then how logging works when the model changes on every question. The second answer shaped the first: `sessionLog.current` keys its file by provider, so a conversation that switches provider writes one file per provider, each holding only its own questions - resuming one file would lose the rest.

- `vscode/session-log.js`: a conversation id (`vertex_conversation`) on every entry; `reset()` starts a new one, `reset(id)` keeps the id of a conversation continued from its log. Default file names got a random hex tail: the test showed that two conversations started in the same second appended to one file, which the continuation would then read as one.
- `vscode/log-report.js`: `parseSession` records the conversation id and each prompt's operation; `conversationTurns` gathers every file with the session's id (or the file alone for logs written before ids), keeps Chat and Web search prompts in time order with their last logged answer, and refuses loudly when the questions or the answers were not logged (`[not logged]` counts as absent - the first try took it for an answer). The panel's `continueConversation` message runs `vertex.continueConversation`.
- `vscode/sidebar.js`: that command opens the panel if needed, resets the log under the same id, calls `ask.restoreConversation` (`vscode/chat.js`: a new conversation whose history is the turns) and redraws the questions and answers with a first line saying where they came from and that tool results are not repeated. `vscode/resources/log-report.html`: a **Continue in chat** button on sessions that hold chat prompts.
- `test/continue-conversation.test.js`: two providers and a commit file in one conversation, another conversation kept out, the continued conversation logging under its id; missing answers or questions refused; the chat taking the turns. Full suite: 1306 pass, the four old failures remain (the Vercel live test passed this time).

## 2026-11-08 — Toolsets: extra MCP tools on demand (0.9.71)

The user asked whether VERTEX could orchestrate - switch on SAP's tools when RAP is needed - and said to do it after the design was laid out: VERTEX's tools stay the base, other servers become toolsets the model enables through one small tool.

- `vscode/mcp-external.js`: starting a server is now `plan(entry)` - a key that says whether a running copy fits and a `start` - shared by the MCP-list server and toolsets. Toolsets: `enable_toolset` (offered only when a set exists for a server other than the one picked in the list), `enableToolset` starts or reuses the set's server, filters its tools by the set's glob patterns and errors when none match; enabled sets stay for the session and are stopped with the rest. The wrapper's `schemas` adds `enable_toolset` and the enabled tools (no duplicate names), `execute` routes them to their server, `external` covers them, `mcpNote` lists the sets.
- `vscode/chat.js`: after `enable_toolset` the request's tool list gets the new tools; `vscode/anthropic.js`, `vscode/copilot.js` and `vscode/openai-compatible.js` read the tool list again at every step (the OpenAI-compatible one keeps `submit_vertex_answer` last and leaves a text-only or web-search request alone). Claude Code and Codex register the tools at the start of a request, so for them a set joins from the next question; the tool's description and result say so.
- `vscode/package.json`: `vertex.chat.toolsets` with the default SAP RAP set (11 SAP tools, about 21 KB of descriptions against about 93 KB for the whole server) and a note telling the model to list destinations, name the one it uses and say which system it changed.
- Tests: `test/mcp-toolsets.test.js` runs a miniature Streamable HTTP server (event-stream and JSON answers, session id, bearer token) through offering, enabling, routing, a set's unknown name and a refused token; `test/toolset-rounds.test.js` checks that an OpenAI-compatible request offers the new tools on the next step. `test/git-history.test.js` expected the small review icon on the Git waiting page, which the wide scene replaced earlier today; it now checks for the generation strip. Full suite: 1302 pass, the same four old failures and the Vercel live request without a key.
- Checked live against SAP's server: enabling SAP RAP took about 0.1 s and `abap_objects_generator_list` returned the generators.

- `vscode/git-branches.js`: the shared PR checks moved into `checkPR`; `prSnapshot` reads `git log` and `git diff` from `refs/remotes/<remote>/<base>` to HEAD with a 64 MB buffer, since git-push's 1 MB one would fail on a large diff, and is cut at 180,000 characters with a marker as the commit snapshot is. A missing remote-tracking branch or an empty range is an error. `prUrl` adds `title` and `body` and refuses an address over 8,000 characters - checked before `ls-remote`. Trial on this repository: a missing base gave its error, the real range gave a truncated snapshot, a 9,000-character body was refused.
- `vscode/code-review.js`: Title, Description and Generate with AI in the PR dialog, the generation strip while it runs; the commit strip in the Push dialog while pushing. `.git-dialog textarea` had no style and rendered as a small box beside its label in the first preview; it now shares the inputs' style.
- The first writing of the new string literals lost one level of `
` escaping and broke `git-commit.js`, `git-branches.js` and the webview script; fixed by hand. Full suite: 1296 of 1301, the same five failures as before. Both dialogs checked in a static preview with a dark theme.

The user asked for each server's write settings in the start window itself: keep the default or tick another, and find it later in the ordinary settings.

## 2026-11-08 — Chat SAP tools from ARC-1 or mcp-abap-adt (0.9.71)

The request was to connect ARC-1 to VERTEX. The first guess was a user-scope entry in `~/.claude.json` beside the `vertex` server; it was written with a broken `npx.cmd` path (an escaping slip) and then removed, because the request was for the extension itself. The design settled with the user: an MCP list in the VERTEX panel choosing where the chat's SAP tools come from, servers listed in settings and started through `npx` rather than bundled in the VSIX (Node.js becomes a requirement for this choice only), and ARC-1's write access as a separate setting.

- `vscode/mcp-external.js` (new): a newline-delimited JSON-RPC stdio client, the server registry over `vertex.chat.mcpServers`, `${...}` placeholders filled from the active system and the kept password, and a wrapper over VERTEX's chat tool set. With a server picked, its tools replace VERTEX's SAP tools; `debug_*` and the transpiler stay. The wrapper defines its members with `defineProperty`, because the extension test showed VERTEX's set holds read-only properties. On Windows the command is started through the shell as one quoted string, which avoids Node's DEP0190 warning for shell arguments. The command is checked on the PATH first (`where`/`which`), because cmd's "not recognized" arrives in the system language and in its code page.
- mcp-abap-adt: version 16 and later no longer reads its connection from the environment, and 15.1.0 connected to its `mock` default, so 23.1.0 is pinned and gets a temporary `.env` (`envFile` in the entry, `--env-path=${envFile}`) in the extension's global storage, written readable by the user only, deleted when the server stops and swept at the next activation. It also needed `SAP_CONNECTION_TYPE=http`, and `--transport` is gone from its CLI.
- `vscode/chat.js`: the picked server is started before the request lists its tools; a note in the instructions says VERTEX's tool names are not available then.
- `vscode/extension.js`: the chat tool set is wrapped; the `/chat` endpoint's tools and instructions became getters so Claude Code and Codex see the current server's tools.
- `vscode/sidebar.js`: the MCP list after the client list, and a start window with the install scene, the result, and **Get Node.js** when `npx` is missing.
- `vscode/task-visual.js`: an `install` wide scene in the commit scene's style: a package travels from the registry into the server node, with a pulse and check; theme colours and reduced motion as before.
- `vscode/package.json`: `vertex.chat.mcpServer`, `vertex.chat.mcpServers` (ARC-1 1.10.1 and mcp-abap-adt 23.1.0 by default), `vertex.chat.arc1Access`. A timeout setting was added and taken out again: nobody asked for it.
- Checked live on the development system: ARC-1 `SAPSearch` and mcp-abap-adt `GetPackage` answered, and the temporary `.env` was gone after the stop. The install window was checked in a static preview in dark and light colours. The full test suite: 1296 of 1303 pass; four failures are the same on the unchanged HEAD, the fifth is a live Vercel request without a key.

The user pointed out that agents usually work in their own git copy; so, for a folder in git, `agent-worktree.js` makes a `git worktree` from `git stash create` (the folder's tracked state, uncommitted changes included, HEAD when clean), copies the untracked non-ignored files in, and commits a baseline inside the copy. `changes()` diffs the copy against that baseline and compares blob ids (`hash-object`), so line-end filters do not show as changes; a decided file shows again only when the copy changes it anew; a file whose folder version differs from the baseline is a conflict and `apply()` refuses it. In `chat.js` the copy belongs to the conversation (removed on New conversation and when the panel's extension unloads); Claude runs in it with Edit/Write allowed and only Bash asking; when the answer is done `worktree-review.js` opens `filesReviewHtml` in a new `worktree` mode (Apply instead of Allow, no Deny, a reason box on a declined file, Approve disabled on a conflict, binary and deleted files noted). Apply copies approved files; a declined file with a reason stays in the copy and the reasons are sent through a new `vertex.chatSend` command as the next message, which the panel shows and sends like a typed one; without a reason the copy gets the folder's version back. The outcome is put before the next request. Folders outside git keep the earlier review-before-write. Tests: a real repository for the copy and the review flow. The baseline commits live only in the copy's detached HEAD and go with it. Not tried with a real Claude Code yet. VSIX and Eclipse site rebuilt.

## 2026-10-29 — Saved review first, staleness check after

Opening a saved review waited for `staleness`, which reads every part's versions ("checking whether ... changed since its review was saved"). `review-front.js` now runs the check only when asked: `check=1` puts it in the summary (the assistant's `reviewPath` asks for it, with `build=1`), `check=only` answers `{ stale_check, request, saved_at, stale }` alone. `versions.html` renders the review, leaves a `#stale-check` line and sends the request again with flag `C` (`tool-routes.js` → `check=only`); `showStale` fills the line only when the answer belongs to the review on screen (request and saved_at), and keeps it on the review so coming back from a part or a developer does not check again. ## 2026-10-28 — Record formula through an SAP call's return stop

The record's Formula and Expression for `LS_RESULT-AMOUNT` after a SAP run of ZVERTEX_DEBUG_LAB stopped at `NEW zcl_calc_facade( )->run( )`. SAP stops on the calling line twice - before the call and again when it returns, before the assignment - so `changeOf` attributed the change to the return stop, whose next stop is at the same depth; `called` (`seen - 1 > made`) was false and `returnedBy` never ran. The return stop is no statement of its own, so `changeOf` now replaces it by the call's stop - the earlier stop on the same line and depth, with only deeper stops between and the value unchanged across them - and the ordinary call path follows. `returnedBy` takes the routine's last stop as the one before the first stop back at the caller's depth, not `seen - 1`. A first attempt patched `derive` instead; the user pointed out the return stop is always there and simply irrelevant to the formula, which put the fix in `changeOf`. Without the unchanged-value condition an earlier loop pass of the same call was taken for the call, which the existing loop test caught. That alone did not fix the user's run. Replaying the saved recording (`20261028_083833_ZVERTEX_DEBUG_LAB.vertex-debug.json`) through `recordSteps` and `build` showed the real cause: stop 173 (line 17) carries neither `vars` nor `watch` - the record read no values there - and `recordSteps` carried the 0 of the return stop into it, so the value seemed to change only after line 17 and was pinned on `WRITE`. A detour first merged `t.watch` reads into the values, on the guess that only some stops are read; the user pointed out Steps & values reads every stop, and the recording proved the stop was simply unread, so that was taken out. `recordSteps` now marks each step `read`, and `changeOf` treats unread stops as unknown: the change belongs to the last statement since the last stop read that writes the name (abaplint), else to that stop - here the return stop on line 16, which then becomes the call. On the recording Expression goes through `run` down to the tariff, rate and tax values, each with its recorded value. Why that stop was left unread is not investigated. Both `visual-debug.html` copies changed alike. Two new tests in `record-formula.test.js`; the record-formula and recorded-view tests pass (27), and in the full suite four unrelated tests fail (CLI choice, WebGUI breakpoint, review plan). Then `shown` drops the trailing zeros of a decimal value, and `replay()` calls `showFlow()` 300 ms after the slider settles (not while playing): `withRecordFormula` already built from `replayAt`, but nothing rebuilt it on replay, so the formula stayed that of the last stop. On the recording that left stops 1 and 101 with "not changed in the record"; the user wanted the part already computed shown even before the assignment. `build` now derives the tree from the last stop and marks a node `pending` when the stop it is seen at (`seen`, a call's result only on return) lies after `at`; the first cut compared `stop`, which counted a call's result as there from the call's entry. Pending values are left out; the user asked for colour instead of a word, so `=` is `.rf-assigned` (theme `testing.iconPassed`) or `.rf-pending` (`testing.iconFailed`) in Expression, its statement list (which now lists pending statements too) and Formula's captions. On the recording: stop 1 has 0 green / 47 red, stop 61 23/24, stop 121 37/10, stop 174 47/0. The unread stop 173 (line 17) still showed the root red, though line 16 had run: `seen` is the first stop that read the value. `changeOf` now also returns `after`, the stop after the statement that made the value (taken before the return stop becomes the call), and `pending` compares that; the node's value is still read at `seen`. Steps 171-172 now show the root red, 173-174 green. The statement list then took the formula's style at the user's request: each target with its value in brackets (`named`), the trailing note keeps only where it ran. Eclipse's `vertex-frontend.js` bundle, which carries its own `record-formula`, was not regenerated. Not checked in the VS Code UI, light or dark.

The user then asked whether the long Expression of the facade run is real or repeats. The repeats are real - each modifier writes `amount = amount + amount * x`, so the previous total stands twice and the base price sixteen times - but the formula was wrong: evaluated it gave about 131,890 against the recorded 11,437.83. `pieces` took only the inside of a source that starts with `CONV` and dropped what abaplint keeps after its closing bracket in the same `Source` node, so `weight_kg * CONV decfloat34( price ) * distance_km / 1000` lost `* distance_km / 1000` and the fuel percent lost `/ base_index * coefficient`. It now brackets the converted operands when there are several and goes on after the bracket. Evaluated on the saved recording the Expression gives 11437.82784814437, the recorded value. New test; formula and value-origin tests pass (95).

## 2026-10-26 — Blame in the review built from ADT

The review built from ADT credited every block to the author of the NEW version, and the review page ignored the BLAME_MAP of reviews saved by AVE. `review-live.js` now builds AVE's blame map (`ZCL_VX_POPUP_DIFF=>BUILD_BLAME_MAP`): the versions from OLD to NEW are replayed with the diff of the Versions window, an added line takes the author of the version that added it and a removed line the one that removed it, lines known by text as in AVE; one author over the whole range skips the replay (`SINGLE_RANGE_AUTHOR`). Crediting the version's author was wrong for a chain of transports of copies: every ToC version carries whoever made the copy. The author is now AVE's OBJ_OWNER (`ZCL_VX_VERSION_LIST=>LOAD`): a task version is its task owner's; a K version, or a ToC read back to its K through CORR/MERG, is the owner's of the K's S/R task that carries the object and is the nearest before the version, else of the newest such task. "Carries the object" is an E071 entry of the task starting with the name the part is read through. Feed times (UTC) are compared with E070's local dates as given. A block belongs to whoever wrote most of its added lines (`ZCL_VX_ACR_HUNK_INFO`); `BT_AUTHORS` counts inserted and modified lines per author as `ZCL_VX_REVIEW_STATS=>FROM_DIFF` does, deleted lines on no one, blocks from the review's own blocks. The payload carries `BLAME_MAP`, `BLAME_DELETED` and `KEY-BLAME` in AVE's format. `review-front.js` attaches the author to each changed line and builds the Developers table from `BT_AUTHORS`, an object with two authors appearing under both; `versions.html` shows the name at the right of the line, both in one and in two panes, with version, date and request on hover. Blame costs one source read per version of the range, so it is AVE's switch here too: a Blame toggle (`vertex-toggle`), off by default. It was first drawn inside the rendered summary and part, so it appeared only after a review had been read - too late for the one choice that makes reading slow; it now stands beside the Versions | Review switch in Review mode and asks for the current view again when flipped. Opening a saved review of a large request stood on "Reading ..." with no sign of life: before anything is shown, `staleness` reads the version feed of every part the request holds. It now reports each part through the same progress line a build uses ("checking whether … changed since its review was saved: n of m, part"). A released request is no longer checked: its versions are fixed and its pair comes from its own versions only (0.9.33), so the check could only find later work of other requests, which its review is not about - and for a review saved by AVE it reported every class part as changed, comparing AVE's per-method VRSD numbers with the class include's ADT feed numbers. Rebuild from ADT was drawn only inside the staleness block, so with the check gone a released request lost it - and rebuilding is also wanted when VERTEX's own rules changed, or to rebuild a review saved by AVE. It now stands under the "Saved … by …" line of every saved review (not of one against another system), and the staleness block only lists what moved. The review was read from the first place found - the file first in file mode - and a second copy was never mentioned: on a system without the ABAP backend, the first approval in VERTEX put a whole copy in a file, after which AVE's later verdicts in ZAVE_REVIEW were silently out of sight. `loadStored` now reads both places and the answer carries `copies` (who saved each, when, which file). A `from` parameter (table / file; a seventh argument of `sdeReview` / `sdeAct`, `from=` in `tool-routes.js`) picks the copy; a copy asked for by name that is not there fails instead of showing the other. A write goes back to the copy it read: the table where VERTEX can write it, otherwise the file, which the page states before any write; a new review (Save) still follows the storage setting. Nothing is merged. The page names both copies above the "Saved" line with a `vertex-segment-toggle` Table | File; the pick is kept for its request only. Open requests are still checked that way; that comparison is wrong for AVE-saved class parts and is not fixed here. It travels as a sixth argument of `sdeReview`/`sdeAct`, `blame=1` in the review path (`tool-routes.js`), and on to `review-live.build`, whose cache keeps the two builds apart; a review saved from the page is saved with or without Blame as the toggle stands. Off, nothing is read for blame, blocks keep the NEW version's author and `BT_AUTHORS` is empty; the page also hides line authors and blame-based developers a saved review keeps. The review-missing test now expects a part with no version at all to be listed (the 0.9.33 change), which that test had not been run against.

## 2026-10-26 — Own transports of copies in the review pair

A request review showed for the CCIMP of a class only the difference between the active state and v287, the request's latest ToC; the right base was v272 from another request. `requestParts` collected only the request and its tasks, so `pairOf` treated each ToC version as foreign and took the newest one as OLD. That gap was noted as "Not carried" next to `pairOf`. The request's ToCs are now read from their `CORR/MERG` entries in E071 (as in `ZCL_VX_REQUEST=>RESOLVE_PARENT_K`) and belong to the request's numbers, so they are skipped for OLD and count as the request's own for NEW. A ToC without a MERG entry but with STRKORR set already came in through the tasks query. A focused `pairOf` test covers a ToC chain above the old base. `pairOf` also fell back to the active state for any part with no version of the request, released request or not, so an old request reviewed the work of whoever changed the part since. As in AVE (`IS_RELEASED_KORR`), the fallback now applies only while the request is open (E070 TRSTATUS not R or N); a released request reviews only its own versions, and a part with none has no pair. Such a part, like any part without a pair, was skipped without a word; it is now listed among the parts that could not be read, with the reason, both in the review and in the staleness check. A `pairOf` test covers both states.

New `vscode/reach-path.js`, command `vertex.reachPath` (editor context menu for ABAP, hidden from the palette). Structure comes from abaplint statement kinds (`parserKind` from value-origin-linter's parse of the editor text, unsaved edits included), not from text patterns. One pass from the routine's start to the cursor's statement keeps a stack of open blocks; each branch records its CHECKs, the inner branches that leave, and an unconditional exit. On close, a branch that leaves becomes "must not be taken" in its parent, a branch with conditional exits becomes "if taken:" with them nested; when every branch of a covering IF/CASE leaves, the parent branch itself leaves. CHECK/CONTINUE/EXIT inside a loop are scoped to that loop and dropped when it closes. The open stack then gives the path: earlier branches false, the taken branch true (ELSE/WHEN OTHERS unlabelled), loops entered, CATCH as raised and caught.

Navigation goes through Mermaid `click` directives, and ace-scheme gave them only to conditions, blocks, exits and folds; now every `p` and `j` node gets an `acego_` click at the end, unless it already has one (an exit, an opened operation's `aceexp_`). A fold of one operation became the operation itself ("1 operation" took a box anyway). Scrolling "stuck": a click in the diagram opened the line, the editor scrolled, and its visible-range event carried userFocus (the editor was active) and handed the lead back to the code, which scrolled the diagram; the diagram's own scroll in turn moved the editor. As the user set it: a mouse click decides the lead (diagram pointerdown; editor selection of kind Mouse), scroll events never take it, scrolling the diagram no longer moves the source (that listener removed with its timer state), and the source scrolling into another method still opens that method's diagram even while the diagram leads. The wheel no longer takes the lead. 928 tests pass; not checked in VS Code itself; Eclipse's host sends its own cursor events and was not changed.

The user, on the installed build: operations still not clickable, and after working in the code then turning to the diagram, scrolling pulled it back. The real metrics.html, loaded in the browser with a stub host on the user's method (ZCL_AVE_POPUP=>BELONGS_TO_CLASS), opened the line for every node but the ENDIFs - in VS Code, navigation goes by `data-source-line` from nodeLines, not by the Mermaid clicks, and `j` nodes were missing from nodeLines; they are in it now. The pull-back: opening a line from the diagram changes the active editor, and tools-window posted `codeFocus`, whose handler (`sdeCodeFocus`) handed the lead back to the code - the 700 ms guard after a diagram click is shorter than opening a SAP source can take. By the user's rule only a mouse click changes the lead, so the `codeFocus` chain (tools-window listener and relay, tools.html relay, metrics.html handler) is removed. Why operations seemed unclickable in VS Code itself is not established: in the page they open; the pull-back may have hidden it. 928 tests pass.

Still wrong for the user: "if I scroll, I have grabbed the window". The editor's own moves after a line is opened from the diagram are kept out by the host's quiet time, which now also starts again when the open has finished, as a SAP source can take longer than its 700 ms. Still pulling back after the first click in the diagram. Two more causes were found and the lead model was given up at the user's word ("clicked - positioned"; then "code scrolling may move the diagram, not the other way - only a click"): VS Code repeats selection and visible-range events with nothing moved (on focus changes among others), and every redraw replayed the stored code cursor through sdeCodeCursor with its old userFocus, scrolling the diagram back. Now there is no lead state (`followCode`, its pointerdown/wheel listeners and `userFocus` removed): the editor's real moves - tools-window passes on a selection or visible range only when it differs from the last one, also remembering it during the quiet time after a diagram click - position the diagram; a redraw marks the cursor's node again without scrolling (`replay`), except right after a method opened for the code (`positionAfterDraw`); scrolling the diagram touches nothing. 928 tests pass; not checked in VS Code itself.

## 2026-10-22 — the test suite passes again after the 0.9.21 merge

23 of 918 tests failed. None came from the merge: each already failed on one side or both. Three were code faults.

- `local-trace.js` `abapFailure`: the drive-letter pattern took the `e:` of `file:///` on macOS and Linux, so a failed local run gave Node's stack instead of the ABAP place.
- `pages/visual-debug.html` `stepFlow`: a block a statement stands in was keyed by the routine key (`m|…`), a statement by `stepKey`, so a CASE the run stopped on became two nodes and its WHEN hung from the second. Blocks are now keyed as statements.
- `value-origin-model.js` `fullFlow`: since 0.8.7 the flow enters only routines with a statement of the slice, and that mark came only from ACE flow points. A local analysis has none, so BSE FLOW never left the event. Without ACE points a statement is marked where the backward slice reached a calculation on its line.

The rest were tests: Windows paths built as strings (`local-analysis`, the `sapnwrfc.dll` lookup, now Windows-only), macOS's `/var` → `/private/var` temporary folder (`local-run`), and expectations that recorded decisions had changed: the SAP ADT extension route removed in 0.9.11, Logic-only folding and loop frames (0.8.1), parameter nodes dropped from FLOW (0.8.2), routine frames in Statements (0.8.1), END statements kept with their block (0.8.3), `open_sap_object` in the active group, and the page's current wording. The full suite passes: 917, one skipped off Windows.

## Unreleased — Logic position and ALC function module

The shared Logic diagram reset its viewport on each graph redraw, including Visual Debug record updates. It now fits once and preserves scroll and zoom on later redraws. Generated default binding is applied to the defining group, duplicate importing/exporting names are bound once, and legacy `><` is normalized for the transpiler. The user wants the analyses on a recorded history - transpiler or SAP - without running the program again: pick the step to start from, and choose any variable again and again; "the same as we already compute". What was there: following a value (Variables' menu) rebuilds Formula from the record at the player's stop (`at=replayAt`) and asks the slice; Analyze flow path and Where used start from a breakpoint.
